page: The Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare-metal dedicated server positioned within the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is powered by an 8-core, 16-thread Intel Xeon E-2388G processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz. The CPU features 16 MB of L3 cache, hardware support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI), AES, and SHA-NI, and dedicated thread execution without hypervisor virtualization overhead. The server includes 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU, paired with 3,840 GB of integrated high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU acceleration is included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-core execution. The platform achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2,184.0, ranking in the top 25%, and a PassMark memory score of 3,390.33, placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded compression throughput reached 36.27 GB/sec in gzip testing. In multi-threaded execution, the server produced a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,124.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 23,271.22, both aligning with the middle 50% average across comparable hardware. Memory operations yield strong small-block cached read throughput at 1,099.44 GB/sec, although large uncached block transfers showed lower bandwidth figures of 36.93 GB/sec read and 19.38 GB/sec write.

Application-level performance reflects balanced efficiency for database and web delivery architectures. The configuration sustained 16.84 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.59 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. For edge CPU inferencing workloads, lightweight 135M parameter models executed at 275.61 generation tokens per second, while 7B models reached 9.95 tokens per second. With 128 GB of RAM and 3,840 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage, the machine delivers a cost-efficient bare-metal profile for memory-intensive relational databases, caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, and continuous integration services requiring direct hardware access without virtualization jitter.

Equipped with 128 GB of DDR4 RAM and 3,840 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, it eliminates hypervisor overhead while offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In synthetic and practical testing, it demonstrates strong single-threaded performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,184.0 and gzip compression throughput of 36.27 GB/sec, alongside top-decile PassMark memory results. The platform provides consistent operational throughput for database operations, reaching 16.84 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking a discrete GPU, the server is well matched for bare-metal workloads including in-memory databases, caching services, high-throughput web serving, and enterprise container hosting.
